notes: Derived edit. Planet types are individuals (instance_of). The definitional premise 'a moon orbits a planet of a given type exactly when the planet it orbits is of that type' is a SWRL rule one way (orbits_planet_of_type is functional, so it can't be a chain target) and a class axiom per type the other way, so the premise route reaches an unnamed planet. The direct question ('a terrestrial planet or a gas giant?') presupposes the two types exclude each other (firm disjointness). q1's original 'no' needs a gas giant to lack a solid surface (the record's w2 side fact 'its lack of a solid surface' goes with Jupiter's type).

type_rule: orbits_planet_of_type value gas_giant ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value gas_giant)
orbits_planet_of_type value terrestrial ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value terrestrial)
